rulebook.title: How to play

night.title: Confirm your role at night
night.detail: Everyone acknowledges the first Leader, then privately views their role and night information. Day begins once all confirm.

discussion.title: Round-by-round discussion
discussion.detail: Slow round: everyone may speak freely. Fast round: the leader invites one player for a two-person conversation. The leader may end the discussion early.

team.title: The leader selects a team
team.detail: The leader selects quest members according to the team-size table below.

vote.title: Everyone votes
vote.detail: Players approve or reject the team. A majority must approve to proceed; otherwise a new leader starts another discussion. Five consecutive rejections give Evil the win.

quest.title: Carry out the quest in secret
quest.detail: Team members submit cards secretly. Good must play Success; Evil usually has a choice. The Lunatic must Fail, while the Brute must play Success on quests 4–5. One Fail usually fails a quest.

evilDiscussion.title: Assassination discussion
evilDiscussion.detail: After three successful quests, all roles remain secret. Anyone may speak or reveal their own role.

victory.title: Decide the winner
victory.detail: Three failed quests give Evil the win. After three successes, the Assassin locks in one target: finding Merlin wins for Evil; otherwise Good wins.

rulebook.sequenceHint: Hover over or tap a quest card to see its team size and special rule.
rulebook.night: Everyone acknowledges the first Leader, then privately views their role and night information. Day begins once all confirm.
rulebook.discussion: Each round begins with discussion. In a slow round, everyone can speak for 30 seconds per player. In a fast round, the leader has 15 seconds to invite one player, followed by a 60-second dialogue. Team selection begins when time runs out or the leader ends discussion early.
rulebook.team: The leader selects a quest team of the size shown below. Submitting the team automatically records the leader's approval.
rulebook.vote: Other players secretly approve or reject. The team proceeds only with more than half the votes; a tie rejects it. Five consecutive rejections give Evil the win.
rulebook.quest: Only quest members secretly play cards. Good players must Execute; Evil players may Execute or Sabotage. Usually one Sabotage card fails the quest.
rulebook.victory: Three failed quests give Evil the win. After three successful quests, the Assassin names Merlin: a correct guess wins for Evil, otherwise Good wins.
rulebook.teamSizes: Teams and quest sizes by player count
rulebook.twoFails: With 7 or more players, the fourth quest needs at least two Sabotage cards to fail.

specialRules.title: Special roles and variant rules
specialRules.pair: Good and Evil Lancelot join together, using one Good and one Evil slot.

percival.vision: Sees Merlin and Morgana without knowing which is which. Without Morgana, identifies Merlin.

morgana.vision: Appears alongside Merlin to Percival; still recognises Evil allies.

mordred.vision: Hidden from Merlin; still recognises Evil allies.

oberon.vision: Neither sees nor is seen by other Evil players, but Merlin sees them.

cleric.vision: Privately checks the first Leader’s allegiance, without learning their role.
cleric.check: Always checks the original Leader. The Trickster may report a false allegiance.

lunatic.quest: Must play Fail on every Quest they join.

brute.quest: May play Success or Fail on Quests 1–3; only Success on Quests 4–5.
brute.limit: Uses the Quest number, not the number of successes or failures.

revealer.reveal: Revealed to everyone after the second failed Quest. Quest cards and victory rules stay unchanged.

untrustworthy_servant.vision: Knows the Assassin. Merlin sees them among Evil, but Evil players do not see them as an ally.
untrustworthy_servant.quest: Only Success cards. Loyalty checks use their current actual allegiance.
untrustworthy_servant.recruit: After three successful Quests and Evil discussion, the Assassin gets one recruitment guess.
untrustworthy_servant.outcome: Correct: revealed, becomes Evil and assassinates instead. Incorrect: stays Good and the Assassin proceeds. Final allegiance determines victory.

trickster.check: May report Good or Evil when checked by the Cleric or Lady.
trickster.limit: Lying changes neither actual allegiance nor Quest cards or victory. Recognises Evil allies and is seen by Merlin.

lancelot.fixed: Recognise each other at the start; allegiances stay fixed.
lancelot.night: Do not recognise each other. Initial Evil Lancelot sees no Evil allies; other Evil players, except Oberon, see them.
lancelot.vision: Opening vision stays fixed after switches; no night information is gained or lost.
lancelot.deck: Shuffle 5 cards: 3 No Change, 2 Switch. At most two switches.
lancelot.draw: Draw once without replacement at the start of Quests 3, 4 and 5. Rejected teams cause no extra draw.
lancelot.private: Only the two Lancelots receive results. Switches are never announced publicly.
lancelot.permissions: Currently Good: Success only. Currently Evil: Success or Fail.
lancelot.outcome: A switch swaps current allegiances, never character identities. Final allegiance determines victory.

lady.holder: Starts with the player to the first Leader’s right. Recommended for 7+ players.
lady.timing: Checks after Quests 2, 3 and 4; skipped when the endgame begins.
lady.result: Privately learns the target’s allegiance at that moment, then passes the token to them. The Trickster may lie.
lady.targets: Cannot check yourself or anyone who has used the token. Results do not update after later allegiance changes.
